files.description: Account sign-ups (300 rows, not in date order): account_id (whole number), signup_day (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD, between 2023 and 2025; no empty cells), channel (web, app, referral or partner; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent; about 2% empty), first_payment (amount with two decimals; about 5% empty).

task_text: For each sign-up channel (written in lower case without surrounding spaces; rows without a channel are left out), give the first and the last sign-up day as Unix timestamps in seconds (midnight UTC of that day). `result` should be a table indexed by channel with the columns first_signup and last_signup (whole numbers).
intended_computation: Parse signup_day, clean channel (4 channels), and per channel return the minimum and maximum sign-up day as seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC (values between 2023-01-01 and 2026-01-01, i.e. 1672531200-1767225600).

predicted_direction.reason: on 3.x parsed dates are stored at a coarser unit, so the integer cast divided by 10**9 gives numbers 1000 times too small

notes: Drafted 2026-11-11 in package TASKS_M1; task text, card, naive solution, reference and predicted direction were prepared there.
